finalText:
Migration finished. All 12 remaining non-vendor call sites moved from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

- `packages/accounts` — `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`
- `packages/billing` — `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js`
- `packages/catalog` — `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js`
- `packages/orders` — `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js`
- `packages/analytics` — `repo/cohort.js`
- `packages/support` — `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js`

All files pass `node --check`; there is no test suite in the repo to run.

Two things I deliberately left alone:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js`** (2 calls) — its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local edits silently lost. Migrating it in place would be reverted by the next upgrade. This needs either an upstream fix, a wrapper/shim at the `require` boundary, or dropping the vendored dep — your call which. It's the only thing still holding `db.query` alive outside `lib/db.js`.
- **`cache.query(...)`** calls in the repo files — that's the cache handle, unrelated API, not part of this migration.

`db.query` remains defined in `lib/db.js` because of the vendor usage; once that's resolved you can delete the deprecated method.
